name: Avatime
confidence_why: Schuh 1995, van Putten 2014 and Defina 2016 all describe Avatime as a language with contrastive level tones and tone-only minimal pairs and none states a word-stress rule; the only difference among them is whether the tone inventory has four levels (Schuh 1995, following Ford 1971a) or three (van Putten 2014, Defina 2016).
catalog_citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1995. Aspects of Avatime phonology. Studies in African Linguistics 24(1): 31-67.
catalog_quote: 4.1. Tone levels. Funke [1909:289] and Heine [1968:105] both state that Avatime has three tone levels, plus rising and falling contours. ... Ford [1971a:20] says, "In any utterance, no more than four distinct levels of tone are used ...." He labels the tones with the numbers 1-4, with tone 1 being the lowest. ... My data confirm that Ford is correct in requiring up to four, but no more than four, distinct levels for a description of Avatime tone. ... All native Avatime nouns (and many borrowed nominal roots as well) have a tone bearing prefix. ... With the exception of the ... singular class prefix and the BA, KU, and (L)I plural class prefixes, all of which always bear low tone, the tone of the prefix is a non-predictable feature associated with the specific noun root. Because the tones on these prefixes must be lexically specified, they are sufficient to demonstrate that Avatime has a…

new_statements.quote: Avatime has three contrastive level tones: extra high (which I mark as á), high (unmarked) and low (marked à). The low and high tones are the most frequent tones and occur on all types of words and on different affixes. [...] Some minimal pairs distinguishable only by tone can be seen in (1) [p. 29] Previous work on Avatime has identified four tones: low, mid, high and extra high (Ford, 1971a; Schuh, 1995a). [...] I describe the Avatime tone system with three tones only, as I have not found any instance of the mid tone identified in previous literature. [p. 30]

Section 2.2.2 'Tone' begins on printed p. 29 (p. 42, the text) and the quoted sentences are there verbatim: 'Avatime has three contrastive level tones: extra high (which I mark as á), high (unmarked) and low (marked à). The low and high tones are the most frequent tones and occur on all types of words and on different affixes.' and 'Some minimal pairs distinguishable only by tone can be seen in (1)' (p. 29); 'Previous work on Avatime has identified four tones: low, mid, high and extra high (Ford, 1971a; Schuh, 1995a).' and 'I describe the Avatime tone system with three tones only, as I have not found any instance of the mid tone identifi…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog codes Avatime as tonal on Schuh 1995 (up to four tone levels). van Putten 2014 is compatible with the tonal coding and refines the inventory to three contrastive level tones, explicitly rejecting the mid tone of Ford 1971a and Schuh 1995a after checking with six consultants. On word stress itself the work is silent: no stress statement, no placement, no claim that stress is absent.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Avatime is described as a language with three contrastive level tones (extra high, high, low) with tone-only minimal pairs; contour tones arise from floating tones or merged syllables; a tone-raising process raises unstable low/high tones before high tones. The phonology section (phoneme inventory, tone, syllable structure, vowel harmony, tone raising) has no stress or accent subsection and makes no statement about word stress, prominence or accent; the only 'accent'/'stress' hits in the text concern English pitch accent in the information-structure discussion and reference titles.
new_statements.exceptions: Extra high tone is limited in distribution (not on noun roots except loans, rarely on verb roots, rarely on noun class prefixes); the conjunction lɛ̌ and habitual prefix zɛ̌ have lexical rising tones; tone raising applies in the aorist but not in the progressive or negated aorist, with speaker variation in the potential and intentive moods.
new_statements.identity_note: van Putten 2014 is based on the Vane dialect of Avatime (she notes Vane kasɔị vs Amedzofe kasɔwị, i.e. loss of intervocalic w in Vane, p. 31); Schuh 1995 in the catalog and Ford 1971 describe Amedzofe/general Avatime. No dialect difference in tone type is claimed.

tone_statements.citation: Lehman, Blake. 2024. Topics in Avatime Phonology. PhD dissertation, University of California, Los Angeles (committee co-chairs Kie R. Zuraw, W. Harold Torrence). UCLA Electronic Theses and Dissertations, eScholarship.
tone_statements.quote: The phenomena investigated are (i) the status of the [ATR] contrast in high vowels, (ii) the behavior of the low vowel [a] in [ATR] harmony, and (iii) a tone sandhi process in verbs that is phonologically, morphologically, and lexically conditioned. [...] Chapter 4 examines a process of tone sandhi affecting verbs. This process consists of the raising of the tone of verb roots and prefixes in a scalar fashion. [...] It is shown that the process is conditioned by phonologically, morphological, and lexical information.
tone_statements.locator: author's abstract (eScholarship/OAI-PMH record oai:escholarship.org:ark:/13030/qt2v55n5x1); tone analysis itself in Chapter 4
tone_statements.summary: Lexical level-tone system (dissertation reportedly argues modern Avatime needs four contrasting level tones) with a grammatical/lexically conditioned verb tone-raising sandhi that raises root and prefix tones stepwise and can spread to adjacent words.

tone_statements.citation: Ameka, Felix K. & James Essegbey. 2017. Divergence and convergence among the Ghana-Togo Mountain languages. STUF - Language Typology and Universals 70(2): 245-271.
tone_statements.quote: Like all Kwa languages, GTM languages are tone languages. … Essegbey (in preparation) argues that Nyagbo has four level tones-low, mid, high, and extra high. Earlier analyses of Avatime (Ford 1971; Schuh 1995) also proposed that the language had four level tones. But recent investigations by Defina (2016) and Putten (2014) could only confirm three level tones, suggesting that the fourth tone has disappeared. Tones mark lexical as well as grammatical distinctions. In Avatime, for instance, argument focus is marked by a high tone (Putten 2014).
tone_statements.locator: p. 250, section 2.2 'Tone'; extra-high focus tone p. 261; floating extra high tone of elided ni p. 263, ex. (24) p. 264.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones per recent work (earlier analyses had four; the fourth is said to be lost); tone is lexical and grammatical (focus marked by a high/extra-high tone); elided ni leaves a docking tone.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement on type: every opened description (van Putten 2014 here; Schuh 1995 and Defina 2016 already in the catalog) treats Avatime as a level-tone language with tone-only minimal pairs and none states a word-stress rule. The one difference is the size of the tone inventory: Schuh 1995 (the catalog's deciding source) and Ford 1971a require four levels (including a rare mid tone), whereas van Putten 2014 (and Defina 2016) describe three contrastive level tones and report that no consultant produced the mid tone. This affects the tone description, not the tonal classification. The 2023 sketch could not be opened, so it neither confirms nor contradicts.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim at the stated locator in the Schuh 1995 text we hold (lines 1168-1243, sec. 4.1 pp. 57-58). (2) Deciding source is a dedicated 1995 phonology article in Studies in African Linguistics, open-access and. it is the best available prosodic description short of Ford's 1971 unpublished thesis, which it builds on. (3) Two later independent primaries — van Putten 2014 (held) and Defina 2016 (downloaded now to — both describe Avatime as having contrastive level tones with tone-only minimal pairs and contain no stress/accent section; they revise the inventory from four to three levels, which refines 'the primary-stress rule' wording at most but leaves classification tonal, qv=tonal-OR-pitch accent untouched. (4) No instrumental or stress-specific study of Avatime was found in Glottolog's 14 descriptive refs, MPG PuRe, or UGSp

sources.quote: 'Avatime has three contrastive level tones: extra-high (marked á), high (unmarked), and low (marked à)... Some minimal pairs distinguished only by tone can be seen in (1)...
